findings.reason: The protected source is the conventional greedy construction: start with the ascending permutation, scan maximal D runs, and reverse each corresponding inclusive value block in place. Its run_start, boundary, left, and right names expose the block structure, the sentinel removes special-case cleanup, and no inert candidate is materially justified.

Metadata consistently identifies Premium LeetCode problem 484 and its Python string-to-integer-list contract. The implementation returns a permutation of 1 through len(s) + 1, enforces every I or D comparison, and constructs the lexicographically smallest valid sequence. Linear scan and disjoint block reversals match the manifest's O(n) time and O(n) returned-output space.

The immutable native source is bound to verified submission 2065012161. It and the protected app source use the same ascending range, run_start state, inclusive boundary scan, D continuation, two-pointer block swaps, boundary + 1 update, and final return. Differences are limited to the native class/type wrapper and formatting.

The all-D workloads of lengths 32, 128, and 512 span 16x and force one full block reversal. The protected source passed all 8 correctness cases and all three performance tiers, including the legal 100,000-character boundary. A correct repeated-adjacent-swap control passed every output but failed only the runtime verdict with relative growth exponent +1.20 and an 83.40x largest runtime ratio.

The current-targeted Approach follows the exact ascending initialization, run_start and boundary states, s[run_start:boundary] decrease run, inclusive reversal, sentinel closure, and two-pointer swaps. It proves comparison validity and lexicographic minimality block by block and distinguishes required O(n) output space from O(1) auxiliary space.

The hash-bound modular Reference was checked directly against the authenticated Premium statement. It preserves the permutation range and representation rules, lexicographically-smallest request, both examples and explanations in order, both constraints, and the absence of source visuals, tables, follow-ups, or other later sections.

coverage: Both authenticated Premium source examples appear first and in source order with exact pattern, permutation, and lexicographic facts, and both are explicitly tagged as source examples.
The invented third sample is now a trial and both formerly hidden rows are visible trials. Boundaries cover pattern lengths 1 and 100,000 and both legal symbols I and D.

Visible cases cover all increases, all decreases, alternating comparisons, a middle decrease run, multiple decrease runs, a run at the start, a run at the end, and the maximum-length lexicographically increasing permutation.

An independent stack-flush oracle verified all eight authored results and all three benchmark outputs. A brute-force lexicographic oracle covered every one of the 254 patterns through length 7, and 1,000 deterministic randomized patterns also agreed with the protected source.
All eight correctness cases are visible samples or trials; the unchanged length-32, length-128, and length-512 all-D workloads remain hidden and performance-only in benchmark.json.
